priceSnapshot.note: THE ENTIRE WEEKEND BOUNCE IS GONE. Yesterday's endday report closed at 63,347.0 with a bullish tilt, an ADD that had just fired on two 4H closes above the 4H EMA200, and a recommended resting stop at 62,940 - and it named 63,000.0 as 'the trapdoor if Monday does not open bid.' Monday did not open bid. Price lost 63,000 at 20:45 COT, lost the 4H EMA200 (now 63,252.68) on the 20:00 4H close at 62,871.3, and has printed 62,585.2 - the low of the move and 1.20% below the endday mark. The 62,940 stop level was breached; the desk held no futures, so nothing was stopped, but the level was right. What has NOT happened is the thing that would change the structure: 62,284.3, the 1 August low, is still 0.48% below and still untouched. Session range measured from the 2026-08-02 19:30 COT endday snapshot is 62,585.2 - 63,390.0.

reduceIf.confirmation: The core trims only on a 4H CLOSE below $62,284.3 - the 1 August low, unchanged as the invalidation for a fourth consecutive report because it has still never been closed through. That low stopped 4.90 points above the 62,279.54 magnet that dominated the 1 August map and it has held every probe since. A 4H close beneath it means the range that has contained price for three days is finally broken, and the verified shelves underneath on the current CoinGlass surface are 61,999.35 (336.01K) and then a real gap to 61,246.4 (81.68K) before 60,219.65 (208.46K) - roughly 2.1% of air between the first shelf and the next meaningful one.

addIf.confirmation: The NEXT add - this report has already added, see 'changed' - goes on a tag of $61,999.35, the second measured liquidation shelf at 336.01K, that then reclaims 62,410 on a 15m close. That is the same tag-and-reclaim pattern that worked on 1 August at 62,284.3, and requiring the reclaim is what stops the ladder from catching a genuine cascade. A reclaim of 63,000.0 on a 4H close would be the bullish alternative and would restore the endday thesis, but it is not an add trigger - it is a signal to stop adding lower.

decisionBox.changed: FOUR things changed versus the 2026-08-02 endday report. ONE: the overnight risk that report named happened almost exactly as written. It flagged 'a Monday-open fade through 63,000.0' as the concrete risk and put a recommended stop at 62,940; price lost 63,000 at 20:45 COT, traded through 62,940, and printed 62,585.2. The desk carried no leverage, so the call cost nothing, but the endday spot ADD at 63,347.0 is now 1.20% underwater. TWO: the liquidity map flipped sides. The endday map had its brightest pool ABOVE at 63,915.95 with 621.54K and called the pull UP. The current surface has its heaviest sampled band BELOW at 62,410.05 with 432.17K, only 0.28% from spot, and 63,915.95 no longer reads as the dominant feature - the pull is now DOWN. THREE: a genuine macro shock arrived overnight, and it is not a crypto story. Brent crude is $83.24, down $4.69 or 5.33% from the 07/31 settlement of $87.93, with the US 10-year at 4.694% against a 4.740% previous close and DXY at 99.79 from 99.91. Falling oil, falling yields and a softer dollar together is a growth-scare configuration, not a liquidity-easing one, and BTC is trading it as risk-off. FOUR: positioning has flipped short again. CoinGlass 24h Long/Short is 47.47%/52.53% (skew 0.90) against 49.48%/50.52% (skew 0.98) at endday, and 24h liquidations collapsed to $120,950,705 from $146,556,374, down 53% on their own 24h measure. The crowd is leaning short into a support that has held three times - which is the single strongest argument against pressing the downside here.

atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC over 60 sessions through the in-progress 2026-08-03 UTC candle, seeded on a 14-bar simple average of true range then Wilder-smoothed. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), then ATR = (ATRprev x 13 + TR) / 14. ATR has EXPANDED from the 2026-08-02 reading of 1,508.22 to 1,555.69 (+3.1%), reversing two consecutive contractions, because the in-progress 2026-08-03 candle has already covered 63,587.2 - 62,585.2 = $1,002 with most of the UTC day still to run. At 2.49% of spot a normal day covers about $1,556. This is the number that governs today's sizing discipline: the desk's last leveraged trade died on a 416-point stop worth 0.26 ATR, and 62,585 to 62,284 is only 301 points, or 0.19 ATR - which is why today's expression is spot with no stop rather than futures with one.

calibration.rollingRecord: The endday report got the RISK right and the DIRECTION wrong, which is the reverse of the previous three sessions. It wrote that the concrete overnight risk was 'a Monday-open fade through 63,000.0' and recommended a resting stop at 62,940; both levels were hit, in that order, within five hours. But it also carried a bullish tilt at 35/42/23 and acted on it with a spot ADD at 63,347.0, which is now 1.20% underwater at 62,585.2. The reduce level at 62,284.3 did NOT fire - it has still never been closed through on a 4H basis, a fourth consecutive session in which that level has been correctly identified. The published add trigger (a 4H close above the 4H EMA200) fired at endday and was then invalidated one candle later when the 20:00 4H closed 62,871.3 back below it. Scored strictly: the level work was right again, the tilt was wrong, and because the expression was unleveraged spot rather than futures the cost of being wrong was 1.20% of a small tranche instead of a stop-out. That is the lesson from 1 August working as intended.
calibration.note: Two things to carry forward. FIRST, the endday report's own overnight-risk paragraph was a better predictor than its probability table - it named 63,000 as the trapdoor while assigning only 23% to bearish. When the narrative risk section and the probability distribution disagree, the narrative has now been right twice running, and the distribution should be pulled toward it. This report acts on that: bearish is raised from 23% to 34%. SECOND, the add trigger fired on a 4H close above a level and was undone by the very next 4H close. A single 4H close above an EMA200 that sits 30 points from the EMA20 is not a structural reclaim, it is noise inside a compressed shelf. Future add rules anchored on the 4H EMA200 should require the EMA20 and EMA200 to be separated, or require two closes plus a held retest, before being treated as confirmation.
